newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Mannesmann eyes stake in Israeli concern.
newsitem.headline: Mannesmann eyes stake in Israeli concern.

text.p: Germany's Mannesmann AG is in negotiations with Koor Industries to become a strategic partner in the Israeli company's United Steel Mills unit, financial sources said on Monday.
They said the German company would acquire an unspecified holding in United Steel, a manufacturer of steel reinforcement bars, wire rods and wire mesh for the building industry.
Koor's spokesman Amiram Fleisher declined to comment on the report, but the Israeli newspaper Maariv reported that a senior Mannesmann delegation visited Israel three weeks ago.

Koor, Israel's largest holding company, controls 70 percent of United Steel, with the rest publicly traded. United Steel had revenues of 478 million shekels ($141 million) last year, with net earnings of seven million shekels.
Its market capitalisation on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange is just over $40 million.
Bringing Mannesmann in as a strategic partner would be in line with Koor's strategy of forging alliances for its group companies with leading multinational concerns.

In the last two years Koor has sold stakes in its Telrad Telecommunications and Electronic Industries unit to Nortel, its Mercavim bus manufacturing business to Volvo and a toiletries business to Henkel.

Earlier this month, Koor sold 25.1 percent of its Phoencia Glass Works Ltd to Canada's Consumers Packaging Inc. In February, Koor and ITT Sheraton signed an agreement forming a joint venture hotel-management company.
Koor is reportedly in negotiations with several foreign cement companies to take a 20 percent stake in its Nesher Cement unit, which it controls jointly with Clal Israel.
